title: How to measure a vending retail media campaign
excerpt: Build a vending campaign report that distinguishes playback, customer response and product sales, with practical measurement checks.
opening: Plan three lines of evidence. Playback logs describe the creative that ran. Tagged landing-page visits can show trackable responses. Stock and sales records can describe what happened at the machine. Each measure answers a different question, so agree on definitions before the first campaign day.
checklist: Build a sheet with machine ID, site, dates, campaign format, SKU and a reporting owner. Use consistent IDs across media and stock records.
Confirm what a playback log records and how downtime is flagged. Keep play counts separate from estimated audience reach.
If the creative uses a QR code, assign campaign or location tags to the destination URL. Test that the landing page opens and the visit records in analytics.
Capture units sold and in-stock machine-days. Also show total sales across the scheduled period so stockouts remain visible.
If you want to assess incremental sales, plan a comparable baseline or comparison site. Account for changes in price, hours, stock and other promotions.
Give the final report a short limitations section. Separate observed results, plausible explanations and the decision for the next campaign.
close: As an illustrative comparison, 120 sales over 10 in-stock machine-days is 12 per in-stock day. Report that alongside the full campaign dates and any gaps. A playback log alone cannot establish who saw the creative or what caused a sale.
